T0.scene_summary: A small tiled room with a bed in the foreground, white shelving and a cabinet along the back wall, two floor lamps, and an open wooden door.
T0.overall_evidence: The principal furniture and their broad arrangement are recognizable, but the viewpoint and framing differ substantially. The reconstruction also simplifies the cabinet, floor and lighting, and loses several visible surface and furniture details.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction uses a lower, wider-looking framing: the bed is larger and extends across more of the foreground, the door appears narrower and farther back, and the left window and right-side furniture are more heavily cropped.
main_defects.evidence: In the reference the open door dominates the center-right and the bed starts around the lower middle; in the reconstruction the door is a slim strip near the center and the mattress occupies much of the lower right.
main_defects.uncertainty: Differences in object size and placement may also contribute; the images alone do not isolate camera parameters.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction replaces the varied reference surfaces with largely flat gray and white materials; the mottled tan and gray floor, warmer wood grain, and greenish wall tint are notably reduced.
main_defects.evidence: The reference floor has distinct tan and dark irregular patches and the door has visible pale wood variation; the reconstruction floor is uniformly gray and the door nearly uniform pale beige.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent color differences may arise from lighting or rendering rather than material alone.

main_defects.description: The strong warm lamp illumination and contrasting shadows in the reference are absent or greatly diminished in the reconstruction.
main_defects.evidence: The rear lamp in the reference creates bright warm pools above and below its shade, whereas the reconstruction wall is evenly lit with no comparable glow.
main_defects.uncertainty: Exposure and tone mapping may account for part of the difference.

main_defects.description: The cabinet's upper front reads as opaque outlined panels rather than the reference's visibly transparent glazed doors with dark interior shelving.
main_defects.evidence: The reference cabinet has two dark see-through upper panes and visible horizontal shelves; the reconstructed upper fronts are nearly solid white.
main_defects.uncertainty: The panes might be present but rendered too opaque or low-contrast to see.

main_defects.description: The visible door leaf is much narrower in the reconstruction, and its panel detailing is less prominent.
main_defects.evidence: The reference door spans a substantial center-right portion of the frame with large recessed panels; the reconstruction shows a much slimmer pale leaf.
main_defects.uncertainty: The difference may be partly due to viewing angle, door opening angle, or framing rather than physical width.

strengths: The white multi-tier shelving, adjacent narrow cabinet, and two slender floor lamps are present in the correct broad arrangement.
The foreground bed, open paneled door, tiled walls, and right-side white furniture establish the same room layout.
The reconstruction captures the pale palette and simple white furniture forms.
T0.uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Only the two supplied views are available; occluded geometry and exact dimensions cannot be assessed, and camera, lighting and materials can produce overlapping visual differences.

main_defects.evidence: The reference door dominates the center-right foreground, while the reconstruction door sits against the back wall; the bed and wall boundaries also project differently.
